blocks.explanation:
Yeh square-root function ka sawal hai. Yahan koi aik number nahin nikaalna, balke poora graph banana hai.
Is ke liye chaar cheezein chahiye: domain (kaun se x allowed hain), range (kaun se y aa sakte hain), pakke points ki table, aur intercepts.
Plan: square root ke andar wali cheez (radicand) negative nahin ho sakti, is se domain milta hai; x aise chunenge ke radicand perfect square ho (0, 1, 4, 9, 16), taa ke y poore number aayein; phir points laga kar smooth curve se jor denge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \sqrt{3x}\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka graph, domain, range aur intercepts ke saath.
Tareeqa: \(3x \ge 0\) se domain, phir aisi table jis mein \(3x\) perfect square ho, phir points laga kar smooth curve.

Domain
\[3x \ge 0 \Rightarrow x \ge 0\]
Domain \(= [0, \infty)\).
Kyun: negative number ka square root real number nahin hota. Is liye root ke andar wali cheez \(3x\) zero ya positive honi chahiye, yani \(x\) bhi zero ya positive. Graph y-axis ke left mein bilkul nahin jayega.

Range
\(\sqrt{3x} \ge 0\), aur \(x\) barhne se yeh bhi barhta jata hai.
Range \(= [0, \infty)\).
Kyun: \(\sqrt{\ }\) ka nishaan hamesha non-negative (zero ya positive) root deta hai, is liye y kabhi negative nahin hoga. Graph x-axis ke neeche nahin jayega.

Table (\(3x = 0, 1, 4, 9, 36\) banayein)
\[x:\ 0,\ \tfrac{1}{3},\ \tfrac{4}{3},\ 3,\ 12\]
\[y:\ 0,\ 1,\ 2,\ 3,\ 6\]
Kyun: agar hum \(x = 1, 2\) jaise values lete to \(\sqrt{3}, \sqrt{6}\) jaise mushkil decimals aate. Is liye ulta sochte hain: pehle \(3x\) ko perfect square bana do, phir \(x\) nikaal lo. Is tarah har y poora number aata hai aur point bilkul sahi lagta hai.

Intercepts
\[x = 0 \Rightarrow y = 0\]
\[y = 0 \Rightarrow 3x = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0\]
Graph dono axes ko sirf origin \((0, 0)\) par milta hai.
Kyun: y-axis par \(x = 0\) aur x-axis par \(y = 0\) hota hai; dono soorton mein jawab origin hi aata hai.

Graph banayein
Points \((0, 0),\ (\tfrac{1}{3}, 1),\ (\tfrac{4}{3}, 2),\ (3, 3),\ (12, 6)\) laga kar jorein. Curve origin se shuru hoti hai, shuru mein tez charhti hai aur phir dheemi ho jati hai: jaise parabola ka aadha hissa pehlu ke bal leta ho.
Kyunke \(\sqrt{3x} = \sqrt{3}\,\sqrt{x}\), yeh \(y = \sqrt{x}\) wala graph hi hai jo upar ki taraf \(\sqrt{3} \approx 1.73\) guna khench gaya hai (vertical stretch).
Kyun: points ko ruler se seedhe tukron mein nahin, haath se smooth curve bana kar jorte hain, kyunke function plotted points ke darmiyan bhi aahista aahista badalta hai, achanak mor nahin leta.

Tasdeeq
\[x = 3:\ y = \sqrt{9} = 3 \;\checkmark\]
\[x = 12:\ y = \sqrt{36} = 6 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: table ki values wapis function mein rakh kar dekh liya; jawab wohi aaya, is liye points curve par hi hain.
blocks.final_answer: Graph ban gaya: \((0, 0)\) se shuru ho kar right ki taraf \((3, 3)\) aur \((12, 6)\) se guzarta hai; domain \([0, \infty)\), range \([0, \infty)\); sirf origin intercept hai.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = square root of 3x: a half-parabola on its side starting at the origin and rising through (1/3, 1), (4/3, 2), (3, 3) and (12, 6).
answer_figure.caption: Question 3 (i): the graph with its table points and intercepts (original drawing)

Yeh square-root function ka sawal hai. Yahan koi aik number nahin nikaalna, balke poora graph banana hai.
Is ke liye chaar cheezein chahiye: domain (kaun se x allowed hain), range (kaun se y aa sakte hain), pakke points ki table, aur intercepts.
Plan: square root ke andar wali cheez (radicand) negative nahin ho sakti, is se domain milta hai; x aise chunenge ke radicand perfect square ho (0, 1, 4, 9, 16), taa ke y poore number aayein; phir points laga kar smooth curve se jor denge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \sqrt{x} + 5\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka graph, domain, range aur intercepts ke saath.
Tareeqa: \(x \ge 0\) se domain, perfect squares wali table, phir smooth curve.

Domain
\[x \ge 0\]
Domain \(= [0, \infty)\).
Kyun: root ke andar sirf \(x\) hai, aur woh negative nahin ho sakta. Dhyan dein: \(+5\) root ke bahar hai, is liye domain par is ka koi asar nahin.

Range
\[\sqrt{x} \ge 0 \Rightarrow \sqrt{x} + 5 \ge 5\]
Range \(= [5, \infty)\).
Kyun: \(\sqrt{x}\) kam se kam 0 hai; is mein 5 jama karein to jawab kam se kam 5 hoga. Yani graph kabhi \(y = 5\) se neeche nahin aata.

Table (\(x = 0, 1, 4, 9, 16\))
\[x:\ 0,\ 1,\ 4,\ 9,\ 16\]
\[y:\ 5,\ 6,\ 7,\ 8,\ 9\]
Kyun: perfect squares ka root poora number hota hai (\(\sqrt{9} = 3\)), is liye har point pakka aur aasaan hai.

Intercepts
\[x = 0 \Rightarrow y = 5\]
y-intercept \((0, 5)\).
\[y = 0 \Rightarrow \sqrt{x} = -5\]
Yeh na-mumkin hai, is liye koi x-intercept nahin.
Kyun: square root kabhi negative nahin hota, is liye \(\sqrt{x} = -5\) ka koi hal nahin. Graph x-axis tak pohanchta hi nahin; yeh range \([5, \infty)\) se bhi saaf hai.

Graph banayein
Points \((0, 5),\ (1, 6),\ (4, 7),\ (9, 8),\ (16, 9)\) laga kar jorein. Curve \((0, 5)\) se shuru hoti hai aur right ki taraf aahista aahista upar jati hai.
Yeh \(y = \sqrt{x}\) ka graph hi hai, bas poora 5 units upar khisak gaya hai (vertical shift). Root ke bahar jama kiya gaya number graph ko upar ya neeche le jata hai.
Kyun: points ko ruler se seedhe tukron mein nahin, haath se smooth curve bana kar jorte hain, kyunke function plotted points ke darmiyan bhi aahista aahista badalta hai, achanak mor nahin leta.

Tasdeeq
\[x = 9:\ y = 3 + 5 = 8 \;\checkmark\]
Table ki har y-value 5 ya us se zyada hai, jaisa range ne bataya tha.
Kyun: table, domain aur range teeno aapas mein mil rahe hain, is liye graph sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer: Graph ban gaya: \((0, 5)\) se shuru ho kar \((4, 7)\) aur \((16, 9)\) se guzarta hai; domain \([0, \infty)\), range \([5, \infty)\); y-intercept \((0, 5)\), x-intercept koi nahin.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = square root of x plus 5: starts at (0, 5) and rises slowly through (1, 6), (4, 7), (9, 8) and (16, 9).
answer_figure.caption: Question 3 (ii): the graph with its table points and intercepts (original drawing)

steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = -\dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{x}\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka graph, domain, range aur intercepts ke saath.
Tareeqa: \(x \ge 0\) se domain, perfect squares wali table, phir smooth curve.

Domain
\[x \ge 0\]
Domain \(= [0, \infty)\).
Kyun: root ke andar \(x\) hai jo negative nahin ho sakta. Bahar ka \(-\tfrac{1}{2}\) domain ko nahin badalta, sirf y-values ko badalta hai.

Range
\[\sqrt{x} \ge 0 \Rightarrow -\dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{x} \le 0\]
Range \(= (-\infty, 0]\).
Kyun: zero ya positive number ko negative number \(-\tfrac{1}{2}\) se zarb dein to jawab zero ya negative hota hai. Inequality ko negative number se multiply karne par nishaan ulat jata hai (\(\ge\) se \(\le\)).
Dhyan dein: yahi sab se aam ghalti hai; nishaan ulatna na bhoolein.

Table (\(x = 0, 1, 4, 9, 16\))
\[x:\ 0,\ 1,\ 4,\ 9,\ 16\]
\[y:\ 0,\ -\tfrac{1}{2},\ -1,\ -\tfrac{3}{2},\ -2\]
Kyun: perfect squares se pakki values milti hain; misaal ke taur par \(x = 9\) par \(\sqrt{9} = 3\), aur \(-\tfrac{1}{2} \times 3 = -\tfrac{3}{2}\).

Intercepts
\[x = 0 \Rightarrow y = 0\]
\[y = 0 \Rightarrow \sqrt{x} = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0\]
Sirf origin \((0, 0)\) intercept hai.
Kyun: dono shartein aik hi point par le jati hain, is liye graph axes ko sirf origin par chhoota hai.

Graph banayein
Points \((0, 0),\ (1, -0.5),\ (4, -1),\ (9, -1.5),\ (16, -2)\) laga kar jorein. Curve origin se shuru ho kar right ki taraf aahista aahista neeche jati hai, poori x-axis ke neeche.
Yeh \(y = \sqrt{x}\) ka graph hai jo minus sign ki wajah se x-axis mein ulta (reflect) ho gaya, aur \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) ki wajah se aadhi unchai ka reh gaya. Socho jaise aaine mein x-axis ke neeche us ka aks bana ho.
Kyun: points ko ruler se seedhe tukron mein nahin, haath se smooth curve bana kar jorte hain, kyunke function plotted points ke darmiyan bhi aahista aahista badalta hai, achanak mor nahin leta.

Tasdeeq
\[x = 16:\ y = -\tfrac{1}{2}(4) = -2 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: yeh value table se milti hai aur range \((-\infty, 0]\) ke andar hai, is liye graph sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer: Graph ban gaya: \((0, 0)\) se shuru ho kar \((4, -1)\) aur \((16, -2)\) se guzarta hua neeche jata hai; domain \([0, \infty)\), range \((-\infty, 0]\); sirf origin intercept hai.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = minus one half times square root of x: starts at the origin and falls slowly through (1, -0.5), (4, -1), (9, -1.5) and (16, -2).
answer_figure.caption: Question 3 (iii): the graph with its table points and intercepts (original drawing)

steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = -\sqrt{x + 1} + 2\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka graph, domain, range aur intercepts ke saath.
Tareeqa: \(x + 1 \ge 0\) se domain, aisi table jis mein \(x + 1\) perfect square ho, phir smooth curve.

Domain
\[x + 1 \ge 0 \Rightarrow x \ge -1\]
Domain \(= [-1, \infty)\).
Kyun: root ke andar \(x + 1\) hai, jo negative nahin ho sakta. Is liye graph \(x = -1\) se shuru hota hai, us se left mein kuch nahin.
Dhyan dein: \(x + 1 \ge 0\) ka matlab \(x \ge -1\) hai, \(x \ge 1\) nahin; sign ka khayal rakhein.

Range
\[\sqrt{x + 1} \ge 0 \Rightarrow -\sqrt{x + 1} \le 0\]
\[-\sqrt{x + 1} + 2 \le 2\]
Range \(= (-\infty, 2]\).
Kyun: minus sign root wale hisse ko zero ya negative bana deta hai, aur phir 2 jama karne se poori value zyada se zyada 2 rehti hai. Yani graph ka sab se ooncha point \(y = 2\) par hai.

Table (\(x + 1 = 0, 1, 4, 9, 16\) banayein)
\[x:\ -1,\ 0,\ 3,\ 8,\ 15\]
\[y:\ 2,\ 1,\ 0,\ -1,\ -2\]
Kyun: root ke andar perfect square ho to poora number aata hai; misaal: \(x = 8\) par \(x + 1 = 9\), \(\sqrt{9} = 3\), aur \(-3 + 2 = -1\). Pehle radicand chuno, phir us se \(x\) nikaalo.

Intercepts
\[x = 0 \Rightarrow y = -1 + 2 = 1\]
y-intercept \((0, 1)\).
\[y = 0 \Rightarrow \sqrt{x + 1} = 2\]
\[x + 1 = 4 \Rightarrow x = 3\]
x-intercept \((3, 0)\).
Kyun: \(\sqrt{x + 1} = 2\) ke dono taraf square karne se root khatam ho jata hai. 2 positive hai, is liye yeh hal sahi hai (agar right side negative hoti to koi hal na hota).

Graph banayein
Points \((-1, 2),\ (0, 1),\ (3, 0),\ (8, -1),\ (15, -2)\) laga kar jorein. Curve \((-1, 2)\) se shuru ho kar right ki taraf neeche aati hai aur x-axis ko \((3, 0)\) par kaat-ti hai.
Transformations ki zabaan mein: \(y = \sqrt{x}\) ko 1 unit left khiskaya (andar \(+1\)), phir x-axis mein ulta kiya (bahar minus), phir 2 units upar kiya (bahar \(+2\)). Yaad rakhiye: andar ka number ulti taraf le jata hai, \(+1\) yani left.
Kyun: points ko ruler se seedhe tukron mein nahin, haath se smooth curve bana kar jorte hain, kyunke function plotted points ke darmiyan bhi aahista aahista badalta hai, achanak mor nahin leta.

Tasdeeq
\[x = 3:\ y = -\sqrt{4} + 2 = 0 \;\checkmark\]
\[x = 15:\ y = -4 + 2 = -2 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: intercept aur aik door ka point dono equation ko poora karte hain, is liye graph sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer: Graph ban gaya: \((-1, 2)\) se shuru ho kar \((0, 1)\), \((3, 0)\) aur \((15, -2)\) se guzarta hua neeche jata hai; domain \([-1, \infty)\), range \((-\infty, 2]\); y-intercept \((0, 1)\), x-intercept \((3, 0)\).

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = minus square root of (x + 1) plus 2: starts at (-1, 2) and falls through (0, 1), (3, 0), (8, -1) and (15, -2).
answer_figure.caption: Question 3 (iv): the graph with its table points and intercepts (original drawing)

blocks.explanation:
Yeh cube-root function ka sawal hai; is ka graph banana hai.
Domain, range, pakke points ki table aur intercepts chahiye.
Plan: cube root har real number ka hota hai, negative ka bhi (jaise \(\sqrt[3]{-8} = -2\)), is liye domain poora \(\mathbb{R}\) hai. x aise chunenge ke radicand perfect cube ho (\(-8, -1, 0, 1, 8, 27\)), phir points laga kar smooth curve banayenge.
Yaad rakhiye: square-root graph aik point se shuru ho kar sirf aik taraf jata hai, jabke cube-root graph dono taraf hamesha chalta rehta hai aur S-shape banata hai. Yeh farq zehen mein ho to graph ki shakal pehle se andaza ho jati hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \sqrt[3]{2x + 1}\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka graph, domain, range aur intercepts ke saath.
Tareeqa: har real number ka real cube root hota hai; aisi table jis mein \(2x + 1\) perfect cube ho; phir smooth curve.

Domain
\(2x + 1\) koi bhi real number ho sakta hai.
Domain \(= \mathbb{R} = (-\infty, \infty)\).
Kyun: square root ke bar-aks, cube root negative number ka bhi hota hai, jaise \(\sqrt[3]{-8} = -2\) kyunke \((-2)^3 = -8\). Is liye koi x-value mana nahin.
Dhyan dein: square root wala domain ka rule yahan na lagayein; cube root par koi pabandi nahin.

Range
Range \(= \mathbb{R}\).
Kyun: \(2x + 1\) har real value le sakta hai, is liye us ka cube root bhi har real value leta hai: bohat bara negative se bohat bara positive tak.
Dhyan dein: square-root graph ki tarah yahan graph kisi point par shuru ya khatam nahin hota; table mein negative x-values zaroor shamil karein, warna graph ka left hissa reh jayega.

Table (\(2x + 1 = -8, -1, 0, 1, 8, 27\) banayein)
\[x:\ -\tfrac{9}{2},\ -1,\ -\tfrac{1}{2},\ 0,\ \tfrac{7}{2},\ 13\]
\[y:\ -2,\ -1,\ 0,\ 1,\ 2,\ 3\]
Kyun: \(2x + 1 = k\) se \(x = \tfrac{k - 1}{2}\) milta hai. Agar \(k\) perfect cube ho to y poora number aata hai. Misaal: \(k = 8\) se \(x = \tfrac{7}{2}\) aur \(y = 2\).

Intercepts
\[x = 0 \Rightarrow y = \sqrt[3]{1} = 1\]
y-intercept \((0, 1)\).
\[y = 0 \Rightarrow 2x + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\]
x-intercept \((-\tfrac{1}{2}, 0)\).
Kyun: cube root sirf tab zero hota hai jab andar wala number zero ho; is liye \(2x + 1 = 0\) solve kiya.

Graph banayein
Chhe points laga kar jorein. Curve S-shape ki hai jo left se right upar charhti hai; \((-\tfrac{1}{2}, 0)\) ke paas taqreeban khari (vertical) hoti hai aur dono taraf dheemi ho jati hai.
Yeh \(y = \sqrt[3]{x}\) ka graph hai jo \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) unit left khisak gaya aur horizontal taur par 2 guna sikur gaya; is ka markaz (centre) \((-\tfrac{1}{2}, 0)\) hai.
Kyun: points ko ruler se seedhe tukron mein nahin, haath se smooth curve bana kar jorte hain, kyunke function plotted points ke darmiyan bhi aahista aahista badalta hai, achanak mor nahin leta.

Tasdeeq
\[x = 13:\ y = \sqrt[3]{27} = 3 \;\checkmark\]
\[x = -\tfrac{9}{2}:\ y = \sqrt[3]{-8} = -2 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: markaz ke dono taraf aik aik point check kiya; dono table se milte hain.
blocks.final_answer: Graph ban gaya: upar charhti S-shape curve jis ka markaz \((-\tfrac{1}{2}, 0)\) hai, \((-\tfrac{9}{2}, -2)\), \((0, 1)\) aur \((13, 3)\) se guzarti hai; domain aur range \(\mathbb{R}\); intercepts \((-\tfrac{1}{2}, 0)\) aur \((0, 1)\).

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = cube root of (2x + 1): a rising S-shaped curve through (-9/2, -2), (-1, -1), (-1/2, 0), (0, 1), (7/2, 2) and (13, 3).
answer_figure.caption: Question 3 (v): the graph with its table points and intercepts (original drawing)

steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = 2\sqrt[3]{x} - 3\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka graph, domain, range aur intercepts ke saath.
Tareeqa: aisi table jis mein \(x\) perfect cube ho, phir points laga kar smooth curve.

Domain aur range
Domain \(= \mathbb{R}\), range \(= \mathbb{R}\).
Kyun: \(\sqrt[3]{x}\) har real \(x\) ke liye mojood hai aur har real value leta hai. Usay 2 se zarb dena aur 3 minus karna sirf graph ko khenchta aur khiskata hai, koi value nahin rokta.

Table (\(x = -8, -1, 0, 1, 8, 27\))
\[x:\ -8,\ -1,\ 0,\ 1,\ 8,\ 27\]
\[y:\ -7,\ -5,\ -3,\ -1,\ 1,\ 3\]
Kyun: perfect cubes ka cube root poora number hai. Misaal: \(x = 8\) par \(\sqrt[3]{8} = 2\), phir \(2 \times 2 - 3 = 1\). Aur \(x = -8\) par \(\sqrt[3]{-8} = -2\), \(2(-2) - 3 = -7\).
Dhyan dein: pehle cube root, phir 2 se zarb, aakhir mein 3 minus; tarteeb badlein to jawab ghalat aayega.

Intercepts
\[x = 0 \Rightarrow y = -3\]
y-intercept \((0, -3)\).
\[y = 0 \Rightarrow \sqrt[3]{x} = \tfrac{3}{2}\]
\[x = \left(\tfrac{3}{2}\right)^3 = \tfrac{27}{8}\]
x-intercept \((\tfrac{27}{8}, 0)\), taqreeban \((3.4, 0)\).
Kyun: \(2\sqrt[3]{x} = 3\) se \(\sqrt[3]{x} = \tfrac{3}{2}\) aaya, aur dono taraf cube karne se cube root khatam ho gaya.

Graph banayein
Points \((-8, -7),\ (-1, -5),\ (0, -3),\ (1, -1),\ (8, 1),\ (27, 3)\) aur \((\tfrac{27}{8}, 0)\) laga kar jorein. S-shape curve left se right upar jati hai, aur \((0, -3)\) par sab se tez charhti hai.
Yeh \(y = \sqrt[3]{x}\) ka graph hai jo upar neeche 2 guna khench gaya aur 3 units neeche khisak gaya; is ka markaz \((0, -3)\) hai. x-values \(-8\) se 27 tak hain, is liye x-axis par scale chhota rakhein (1 square = 2 ya 4 units).
Kyun: points ko ruler se seedhe tukron mein nahin, haath se smooth curve bana kar jorte hain, kyunke function plotted points ke darmiyan bhi aahista aahista badalta hai, achanak mor nahin leta.

Tasdeeq
\[x = \tfrac{27}{8}:\ y = 2\left(\tfrac{3}{2}\right) - 3 = 0 \;\checkmark\]
\[x = 27:\ y = 2(3) - 3 = 3 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: x-intercept aur table ka aik point dono equation ko poora karte hain. Is ke ilawa graph par dekhiye ke curve markaz \((0, -3)\) ke gird dono taraf aik jaisi hai: \((1, -1)\) markaz se 2 upar hai aur \((-1, -5)\) 2 neeche; yeh bhi aik achhi tasdeeq hai.
blocks.final_answer: Graph ban gaya: upar charhti S-shape curve jis ka markaz \((0, -3)\) hai, \((-8, -7)\), \((1, -1)\), \((8, 1)\) aur \((27, 3)\) se guzarti hai; domain aur range \(\mathbb{R}\); intercepts \((0, -3)\) aur \((\tfrac{27}{8}, 0)\).

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = 2 times cube root of x minus 3: a rising S-shaped curve through (-8, -7), (-1, -5), (0, -3), (1, -1), (27/8, 0), (8, 1) and (27, 3).
answer_figure.caption: Question 3 (vi): the graph with its table points and intercepts (original drawing)

steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(y = \sqrt[3]{x^2 + x - 2}\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka graph, domain, range aur intercepts ke saath.
Tareeqa: pehle root ke andar wali quadratic ko samjhenge (us ke zeros aur sab se choti value), phir table, points aur smooth curve.

Radicand ko samjhein
\[x^2 + x - 2 = (x + 2)(x - 1)\]
\[\text{least value at } x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[\tfrac{1}{4} - \tfrac{1}{2} - 2 = -\tfrac{9}{4}\]
Kyun: root ke andar aik upar khulne wala parabola hai jis ke zeros \(-2\) aur 1 hain aur vertex \((-\tfrac{1}{2}, -\tfrac{9}{4})\) hai (vertex ka x \(= -\tfrac{b}{2a} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\)). Is liye hamara graph bhi \(x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\) wali khari line ke dono taraf aik jaisa hoga.
Dhyan dein: yeh is exercise ka sab se mushkil hissa hai; andar ki quadratic samajh li to graph aasaan ho jata hai.

Domain aur range
Domain \(= \mathbb{R}\).
\[x^2 + x - 2 \ge -\tfrac{9}{4} \Rightarrow y \ge \sqrt[3]{-\tfrac{9}{4}}\]
Range \(= \left[-\sqrt[3]{\tfrac{9}{4}},\ \infty\right)\), jahan \(\sqrt[3]{\tfrac{9}{4}} \approx 1.31\).
Kyun: cube root tarteeb qaim rakhta hai: bara number ho to us ka cube root bhi bara hota hai. Is liye radicand ki sab se choti value \(-\tfrac{9}{4}\) se y ki sab se choti value \(\sqrt[3]{-\tfrac{9}{4}} \approx -1.31\) milti hai. Upar ki taraf koi had nahin.

Table
\[x:\ -4,\ -3,\ -2,\ -1,\ -\tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[y:\ 2.15,\ 1.59,\ 0,\ -1.26,\ -1.31\]
\[x:\ 0,\ 1,\ 2,\ 3\]
\[y:\ -1.26,\ 0,\ 1.59,\ 2.15\]
Kyun: misaal: \(x = 2\) par radicand \(4 + 2 - 2 = 4\), aur \(\sqrt[3]{4} \approx 1.59\) (calculator se). Yahan perfect cubes aasaani se nahin milte, is liye do decimal tak values theek hain. Values jori jori dohraati hain, kyunke graph \(x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\) ke gird symmetric hai.

Intercepts
\[y = 0 \Rightarrow (x + 2)(x - 1) = 0\]
x-intercepts \((-2, 0)\) aur \((1, 0)\).
\[x = 0 \Rightarrow y = \sqrt[3]{-2} \approx -1.26\]
y-intercept \((0, -\sqrt[3]{2})\).
Kyun: cube root bilkul tab zero hota hai jab radicand zero ho; is liye factors ko zero kiya.

Graph banayein
Points laga kar smooth curve se jorein. Curve upar left se neeche aati hai, \((-2, 0)\) par taqreeban khari ho kar mur-ti hai, \((-\tfrac{1}{2}, -1.31)\) par gol tah (bottom) banati hai, phir \((1, 0)\) par dobara tez mur kar upar right ki taraf jati hai.
Shakal aik chaure 'U' jaisi hai jis ki tah chapti (flat) hai, aur \(x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\) ke dono taraf aik jaisi hai. Intercepts par curve khari is liye lagti hai ke cube root zero ke paas bohat tez badalta hai.
Kyun: points ko ruler se seedhe tukron mein nahin, haath se smooth curve bana kar jorte hain, kyunke function plotted points ke darmiyan bhi aahista aahista badalta hai, achanak mor nahin leta.

Tasdeeq
\[x = 2:\ \sqrt[3]{4} \text{ and } x = -3:\ \sqrt[3]{9 - 3 - 2} = \sqrt[3]{4}\]
Kyun: \(x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\) se barabar faasle wale points (yahan 2 aur \(-3\), dono \(2\tfrac{1}{2}\) door) same y dete hain; is se symmetry ki tasdeeq ho gayi.
blocks.final_answer: Graph ban gaya: chaura U-shape curve, \(x = -\tfrac{1}{2}\) ke gird symmetric, sab se neecha point \((-\tfrac{1}{2}, -\sqrt[3]{9/4}) \approx (-0.5, -1.31)\); x-axis ko \((-2, 0)\) aur \((1, 0)\) par tezi se kaat-ta hai aur y-axis ko \((0, -\sqrt[3]{2})\) par; domain \(\mathbb{R}\), range \(\left[-\sqrt[3]{9/4},\ \infty\right)\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ke answer key (safha 295) mein is sawal ke aath graphs, (i) se (viii) tak, diye gaye hain, jabke sawal mein saat hisse chhape hain. Graphs (i) se (vii) chhape hue hisson se milte hain; graph (viii) (aik aur S-shape cube-root curve) kisi chhape hue hisse ka nahin, us ko nazar andaz kar dein.
